links.targetTitle: The Binance instances are Active with their deposit address

title: Exchange conduits acquire a slippage bound and a second recharge rate two thousand times slower than the slope
content:
The Binance `TransferAssets Rate Limits` carry four lines where every other transfer conduit carries two: "`maxAmount`: 5,000,000 USDC, `slope`: 100,000,000 USDC per day, `maxSlippage`: 0.2%, `rechargeRate`: 50,000 USDC per day" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.14.1.2.4.1), with the USDT direction identical in shape (.14.2.2.4.1).

The slippage bound is explicable and interesting: a transfer has no price, but this conduit is a *trade* — send USDC, receive USDT — executed on an exchange rather than in a contract. Carrying `maxSlippage` into a transfer limit is the Artifact acknowledging that the on-chain action is only the first half of a priced transaction. Notably the Paxos conversions, which are issuer mints at par, carry no slippage bound; the exchange conversions do.

The `rechargeRate` is harder to defend. `slope` is already the regeneration parameter used everywhere in the Artifact, and 50,000 per day against a slope of 100,000,000 per day differs by a factor of two thousand. Either the two govern different buckets — perhaps a separate allowance the document does not describe — or one of the figures is wrong, and nothing in the surrounding text distinguishes those readings.

The wider issue is vocabulary drift. Across the venue types this Artifact has introduced slope, slippage, ticks, fee, supply cap, max yield, maximum exposure, capital ratio and now recharge rate, each arriving with a new venue and none defined in the instance documents themselves. A parameter whose meaning cannot be recovered from the document is a parameter that cannot be reviewed.
description: Binance transferAssets limits list maxAmount 5,000,000, slope 100,000,000 per day, maxSlippage 0.2% and rechargeRate 50,000 per day
